issues.issue: Do intervenor's objections (unfairness; wish to amend the return and claim offsetting deductions) defeat petitioner's sec. 6015(c) relief for 2019?
issues.court: no; petitioner relieved under sec. 6015(c) of the deficiency and penalty attributable to intervenor's business income (IRS conceded)
issues.diagnosis: Framework has no sec. 6015 (election eligibility under (c)(3), allocation of items under (d)(3)(A) as if separate returns). The case also turns on jurisdiction/procedure (intervenor cannot enlarge issues or redetermine the deficiency without a timely petition) and on the IRS concession; no return figures are stated, so no allocation could be computed even with sec. 6015 support.
issues.snippet: the Court agrees, despite intervenor's objection, that petitioner is entitled to relief from joint and several liability under section 6015(c).

notes: Notice: 2019 deficiency $33,028 and sec. 6662(b)(2) penalty $6,474 from unreported wages and nonemployee compensation; not contested and not redetermined by the court, so not encoded as expected.
